Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 1:

﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the speech of she who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾. The verse was revealed concerning Khawlah bint Hakim. It is also said Khawlah bint Tha'labah, and it is said Khawlah bint Khuwaylid. It is also said her name was Jamilah, and she was the wife of Aws ibn al-Samit al-Ansari, the brother of Ubadah ibn al-Samit. Aws made a zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce by which a husband declares his wife to be unlawful to him as his mother's back) against her. Zihar in the pre-Jahiliyyah period entailed a permanent prohibition, so when Aws did this, his wife came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Aws has consumed my youth and I have borne him children, and now that I have grown old and my family has died, he has made zihar against me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see that you have become unlawful to him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not do so. I am alone, and I have no family other than him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) answered her with the same words, and she responded to him, and this was her pleading.

﴿And she complains to Allah﴾. She would say: "O Allah, I complain to You of my condition, my loneliness and my poverty." It is also narrated that she used to say: "O Allah, I have young children by him. If I take them to myself they go hungry, and if I give them to him they are lost." ﴿And Allah hears your dialogue﴾. Al-tahawur is the back-and-forth of speech. A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Glory be to Him whose hearing encompasses all voices. I was present, and some of Khawlah's speech was hidden from me, but Allah heard her words, and the Qur'an was revealed concerning that." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then sent for her husband and said to him: "Can you free a slave?" He said: "By Allah, I do not own one." He said: "Can you fast two consecutive months?" He said: "By Allah, I cannot." He said: "Can you feed sixty needy persons?" He said: "I find nothing, unless the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helps me with a gift and a blessing," meaning a supplication. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helped him with fifteen sa' (of dates), and it is said thirty sa', and he prayed for him. He then made expiation by feeding, and kept his wife.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 2:

﴿Those of you who divorce their wives by zihar (saying to them, "You are to me like the back of my mother")﴾. It is read as yuzahirun, with an alif after the zay and without it, and both with shadda and without it; the meaning is one and the same, namely the uttering of zihar. Zihar on which there is consensus is that a man says to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother." According to Malik, what takes the same ruling is the likening of a wife to any woman who is forbidden to him permanently, such as a daughter, a sister, and all the other women forbidden by blood, by suckling, and by marriage alliance, whether or not the word "back" is mentioned. For example, he says: "You are to me like my mother," or "like the belly of my mother," or "her hand," or "her leg." This is contrary to al-Shafi'i, who holds that all of these are not zihar according to him, because he stopped at the wording of the verse, whereas Malik analogized from it, since he saw that the purpose is the likening of something permissible to something forbidden. ﴿They are not their mothers﴾. By this God refutes those who used to utter zihar and believed it to be real. God informs us that the wife becoming (like a mother) is false, for the mother in reality is only the one who gave birth. ﴿And indeed they utter an objectionable word and a falsehood﴾. God informs us that zihar is objectionable (munkar) and false (zawr). The munkar is that which has no recognized reality, and the zawr is falsehood. He called it a falsehood only because the one who makes zihar makes his wife like his mother, and she never becomes so. Zihar is forbidden, and four things indicate its prohibition. The first is God's statement: "They are not their mothers," for that is a denial of the one who makes zihar. The second is that He called it munkar. The third is that He called it zawr. The fourth is His statement: "And indeed God is Pardoning and Forgiving," for pardon and forgiveness occur only for a sin, and it remains incumbent upon the one who makes zihar until he lifts it through expiation (kaffarah).

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verses 3–4:

﴿And those who divorce by zihar from their wives and then wish to retract what they said — then [the expiation is] the freeing of a slave﴾. Allah made the expiation for zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a husband declares his wife to be like his mother's back) into three types, arranged in order. One may not move to the second until unable to perform the first, nor to the third until unable to perform the second. The first is freeing a slave. The second is fasting two consecutive months. The third is feeding sixty poor people, and the food should be from the staple food of the land, typically eaten there. ﴿Before they touch one another﴾. The position of Malik and the majority is that the word "touching" (al-masis) here refers to sexual intercourse and whatever is less than it, such as caressing and kissing. So it is not permissible for the one who has performed zihar to do any of that until he has made expiation. ﴿That is so that you may believe﴾. Ibn 'Atiyya said: the reference is to the concession of moving from freeing a slave to fasting. Al-Zamakhshari said: the meaning is: that clarification and instruction [is so that you may believe]. This is more apparent, because it is more general.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 5:

﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah﴾ means they contend against and oppose Him. ﴿will be humiliated﴾ means they will be destroyed. It was also said: they will be cursed. It was also said: a man is "kubita" when he remains disgraced. The verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites and the Jews.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 7:

﴿There is no secret conference of three but that He is their fourth﴾. It is possible that "najwa" (secret conference, private speech) here means hidden speech, so that "thalatha" (three) is in the genitive as a modifier of it, meaning a group of people, and "thalatha" is then either an apposition (badal) or a qualifier (sifa). The first (reading) is better. ﴿Except that He is their fourth﴾: meaning by His knowledge and His encompassing. Likewise, He is their sixth, and He is with them wherever they are.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 8:

﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret consultation?﴾ It was revealed concerning a group of Jews who used to hold secret consultations among themselves and make signs to one another about the believers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade them from this, but they returned to it. It was also said that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites. The first view is more probable, due to His saying: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾, for this is the act of the Jews. The best view is that the intended people are both the Jews and the hypocrites together, due to His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who took as allies a people on whom Allah has become angry?﴾ [al-Mujadila: 14]. So the verse was revealed concerning both groups. ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾: the Jews used to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and say, "As-sam ʿalayka, yā Muḥammad" instead of "As-salamu ʿalaykum." As-sam means death, and this is what they intended by their words. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to them, "Wa ʿalaykum." One day ʿĀʾisha heard them and said, "Rather, may death and curse be upon you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Gently, O ʿĀʾisha, for Allah dislikes obscenity and the use of obscene speech." She said, "Did you not hear what they said?" He said, "Did you not hear what I said to them? I said, 'Wa ʿalaykum.'" By His saying ﴿by which Allah has not greeted you﴾ he means His saying, ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen﴾ [al-Naml: 59]. ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ They used to say, "If he were a prophet, Allah would punish us for harming him." So Allah said: ﴿Hell is sufficient for them﴾, meaning it suffices them as punishment.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, secret counsel is only from Satan, that he may grieve those who believe﴾. It was said: it means secret counsel concerning sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger; the description of it by these qualities has been omitted because the first mention indicates it. It was also said: he meant the secret counsel of the Jews and the hypocrites, and this is supported by His saying: ﴿that he may grieve those who believe﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 11:

﴿When it is said to you, "Make room in the gatherings," then make room.﴾ There is a difference of opinion concerning the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse. It is said: it was revealed concerning the seats for war and fighting. It is said: it was revealed because of the crowding of people around the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their eagerness to be close to him. It is said: the Prophet (ﷺ) had some people stand up so that some elders from among the people of Badr could be seated in their places, and then the verse was revealed. Then they differed as to whether it is restricted to the gathering of the Prophet (ﷺ) or is general to all gatherings. A group said that it is restricted, and the plural reading "al-majalis" (gatherings) in the singular form "al-majlis" supports this. The majority (al-jumhur) held that it is general, and the plural reading "al-majalis" supports this, and this is the more correct view. On this view, "al-majlis" in the singular is generic (lil-jins). The making of room that is commanded is widening the space, not standing up; for this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Let no one stand up from his place and then another man sit in it, but make room and widen the space." There has been a difference of opinion as to whether this prohibition of standing up from a gathering for someone is a matter of prohibition (tahrim) or disapproval (karahah).

﴿Allah will make room for you﴾, that is, He will widen for you in His Paradise and His mercy. ﴿And when it is said, "Rise up," then rise up﴾, that is, when it is said to you: "Stand up and rise," then do so. There is a difference of opinion concerning this commanded rising. It is said: it is when they are called to fighting, prayer, or any act of obedience. It is said: it is when they are commanded to stand up from the gathering of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he sometimes liked to be alone, and sometimes a group would sit on until they were told to stand. It is said: the meaning is standing up within the gathering to make room.

﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾. In this there are two opinions. The first: Allah raises the believing scholars by degrees; so His saying "and those who have been given knowledge" is a description of "those who believe," like the saying "The noble scholar came to me," while you mean one man. The second: Allah raises both categories, the believers and the scholars, by degrees. So the degrees, on the first view, are for believers on condition that they are scholars, and on the second view for believers who are not scholars, and also for scholars, but there is a difference between the degrees of scholars and others, which is found elsewhere, such as his (ﷺ) saying: "The virtue of the scholar over the worshipper is like the virtue of the full moon on the night of its fullness over the rest of the stars." And his (ﷺ) saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "The virtue of the scholar over the worshipper is like my virtue over the least of you in rank." And his, peace be upon him, saying: "On the Day of Resurrection the prophets will intercede, then the scholars, then the martyrs." So if they have virtue over worshippers and martyrs, then what do you think of their virtue over all other believers?

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verses 12–13:

﴿When you consult the Messenger privately, offer a charity before your private consultation.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: The occasion of its revelation was that a group of young Muslims frequently engaged the Prophet ﷺ in private consultation without any need, in order to display their status. The Prophet ﷺ was generous and would not turn anyone away, so the verse was revealed imposing strictness regarding private consultation. It was also said: the occasion was that the wealthy overwhelmed the poor in private consultation with the Prophet ﷺ.

This verse is abrogated (mansukh) by consensus. It was abrogated by His words after it: ﴿Are you apprehensive about offering charities before your private consultation?﴾ So God permitted them to consult privately without offering a charity, after He had made the offering of charity obligatory before their consultation with him, peace be upon him.

Scholars differed as to whether this abrogation occurred after the verse had been acted upon or not. Some said: no one acted upon it. Others said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, acted upon it. It is narrated that he had a dinar, which he exchanged for ten dirhams, and he consulted the Prophet ten times, giving a dirham in charity each time. It was also said: he gave a dinar in charity each time. Then God revealed the concession for those who were able to give charity, while for those who could not find it, the concession remained established for them through His words: ﴿But if you do not find [the means], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And Allah has turned to you in forgiveness.﴾ Repentance (tawba) here is intended to mean God's pardoning them for their neglect of the charity they had been commanded to give, or His lightening of it after it had become obligatory.

﴿So establish prayer and give zakat﴾, that is: persist in these deeds which are the foundations of your religious law, rather than the charity you had been charged with at the time of private consultation.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 14:

﴿Have you not seen those who have allied themselves with a people upon whom Allah has become angry?﴾ It was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites (munafiqun) who allied themselves with a people from among the Jews, and they are the ones upon whom Allah became angry. ﴿They are neither of you nor of them﴾ meaning that the hypocrites are neither among the Muslims nor among the Jews. This is like His saying concerning them: ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ [al-Nisa: 143]. ﴿And they swear by a lie while they know﴾ meaning that when the hypocrites were rebuked for the evil of their statements and actions, they would swear that they had not said or done it, although such things had come from them many times, as is recorded in the biographies (al-siyar) and elsewhere.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 16:

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾. The origin of *junnah* (shield, protection) is that which one conceals oneself behind and guards against harm, such as a buckler. It is used here metaphorically, because they used to display Islam so that their blood and property would be protected. It is also recited as *ittakhadhū* with a kasra on the hamza (*ittakhadhū*, "they took").

﴿Shaytan has overcome them﴾, i.e., he prevailed over them and took possession of their souls. ﴿Among the most abased﴾, i.e., among the group of the abased, i.e., with them. ﴿God has decreed﴾, i.e., He ordained and predestined.

﴿Shaytan has overcome them﴾, i.e., he prevailed over them and took possession of their souls. ﴿Among the most abased﴾, i.e., among the group of the abased, i.e., with them. ﴿God has decreed﴾, i.e., He ordained and predestined.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 58, verse 22:

﴿You will not find a people﴾ (the verse): its meaning is that you will not find a believer who loves a disbeliever, even if he is the closest of people to him. This is the state of the believer whose faith is sincere. For this reason the Companions, may God be pleased with them, would fight their fathers, sons and brothers when they were disbelievers. Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah killed his father on the day of Uhud, and Mus'ab ibn Umayr killed his brother Aziz ibn Umayr on the day of Uhud. On the day of Badr, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq called his son out to single combat (al-baraz), and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered him to sit down. It has been said that the verse was revealed concerning Hatib, when he wrote to the polytheists informing them of the affairs of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The best view, however, is that it is general in application. It has also been said that it was revealed concerning those who keep company with the ruler, but this is far-fetched.

﴿They show affection﴾ (yuwaddoona): this is a form of mufa'ala (the reciprocal verb pattern) from mawadda (affection), which implies that the affection comes from both sides.

﴿Whoever opposes God﴾ (man hadda Allah): that is, whoever is hostile to Him and opposes Him.

﴿He has written faith into their hearts﴾ (kataba fi qulubihimu al-iman): that is, He has established it in them, as if it were written.

﴿And strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾ (wa-ayyadahum bi-ruhin minhu): that is, with gentleness, guidance and success. It has been said that the "spirit" refers to the Qur'an, and it has been said to refer to Jibril.

﴿Those are the party of God﴾ (ula'ika hizbu Allah): this stands in contrast to His words, "Those are the party of Satan." The hizb (party) are the group of people banded together around the one to whom they are attributed.
